name: IEC set and reset dependency (S, R)
summary: Dependency labels Sm and Rm: the affected output behaves as if set or reset when the affecting input is active.
description: S and R dependencies specify the internal state of an output when both set and reset conditions could be active together. An Rm input at its internal 1 state makes the affected output react as it would to S=0, R=1; an Sm input does the opposite. At 0 they have no effect.

These labels are used where a storage element must have a defined priority between set and reset. A reader can see from the symbol whether set or reset dominates, which matters in latching alarm and interlock logic.
Plain S and R labels without numbers are the ordinary set and reset inputs of a bistable element. The dependency form only applies when a number follows the letter.
readingNotes: S or R followed by a number is a dependency; without a number it is an ordinary input.
Check which one dominates when both are active.
drawingChecklist: Label affected outputs with the matching number.
State set or reset priority in the logic description.
distinction: An ordinary R input resets the element directly; Rm dependency states the reaction of particular outputs.
